title.en: Volume 3 Book of Later Liang 3: Taizu Annals 3
title.raw: 卷三 梁書3: 太祖本紀三 Volume 3 Book of Later Liang 3: Taizu Annals 3

sentences.zh: 二月戊申，帝之家廟棟間有五色芝生焉，狀若芙蓉，紫煙蒙護，數日不散。

translations.literal: On wushen in the second month, five-colored lingzhi grew between the rafters of the Emperor's ancestral temple, shaped like hibiscus, wreathed in purple mist, not dispersing for several days.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen in the second month five-colored lingzhi sprouted between the rafters of the Emperor's ancestral shrine—lotus-shaped, veiled in purple mist that lingered for days.

sentences.zh: 又，是月，家廟第一室神主上，有五色衣自然而生，識者知梁運之興矣。

translations.literal: Also, in that month, on the spirit tablet of the first chamber of the ancestral temple, five-colored garments naturally formed; those who understood knew the rise of the Liang fortune had come.
translations.idiomatic: That same month five-colored vestments appeared of themselves on the spirit tablet of the first ancestral chamber—those in the know took it as a sign that Liang's fortune was rising.

sentences.zh: 唐乾符中，木星入南斗，數夕不退，諸道都統晉國公王鐸觀之，問諸知星者吉凶安在，咸曰：「金火土犯斗即為災，唯木當為福耳！

translations.literal: During Qianfu of Tang, Jupiter entered the Southern Dipper and for several nights did not withdraw. Wang Duo, Prince of Jin and commander-in-chief of all circuits, observed it and asked star-readers where fortune and misfortune lay. All said: "When metal, fire, and earth invade the Dipper it means calamity; only wood should mean blessing!"
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianfu era Jupiter entered the Southern Dipper and held there night after night. Wang Duo, Prince of Jin and overall commander of the circuits, watched it and asked the astrologers what it portended. All agreed: "Metal, fire, or earth in the Dipper means disaster—only wood should mean good fortune!"

sentences.zh: 」或亦然之。

translations.literal: Some agreed with this as well.
translations.idiomatic: Others agreed.

sentences.zh: 時有術士邊岡者，洞曉天文，博通陰陽曆數之妙，窮天下之奇秘，有先見之明，雖京房、管輅不能過也。

translations.literal: At the time there was a technician named Bian Gang who thoroughly understood astronomy, was broadly versed in the subtleties of yin-yang and calendrical reckoning, exhausted the rare secrets of the realm, and had foresight—neither Jing Fang nor Guan Luo could surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: There was then a diviner named Bian Gang, master of the heavens and of yin-yang calendrics, who knew secrets none could match and saw what was coming—surpassing even Jing Fang and Guan Luo.

sentences.zh: 鐸召而質之，岡曰：「惟木為福神，當以帝王占之。

translations.literal: Duo summoned and questioned him. Gang said: "Only wood is the fortune star; it should be read as concerning an emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Duo called him in and pressed him. Gang said: "Wood alone is the star of blessing—it must be read as the omen of an emperor."

sentences.zh: 然則非福於今，必當有驗於後，未敢言之，請他日證其所驗。

translations.literal: Yet this is not fortune for the present; there must be verification later. I dare not speak of it—please verify on another day what is verified.
translations.idiomatic: "But the blessing is not for today—it will prove itself later. I dare not say more; let another day show whether I am right."

sentences.zh: 」一日，又密召岡，因堅請語其詳，至於三四，岡辭不獲。

translations.literal: One day Duo again secretly summoned Gang and, pressing firmly for details, three or four times, Gang could not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Another day Duo summoned him in private and pressed him again and again—three or four times—until Gang could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 鐸乃屏去左右，岡曰：「木星入斗，帝王之兆也。

translations.literal: Duo then dismissed those nearby. Gang said: "Jupiter entering the Dipper is an omen of emperorship."
translations.idiomatic: Duo sent attendants away. Gang said: "Jupiter in the Dipper is the sign of a Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 木在斗中，『朱』字也。

translations.literal: Wood within the Dipper is the character "Zhu."
translations.idiomatic: "Wood inside the Dipper forms the character Zhu."

sentences.zh: 以此觀之，將來當有朱氏為君者也，天戒之矣。

translations.literal: Viewed thus, hereafter there will be one surnamed Zhu as ruler—Heaven has warned of it.
translations.idiomatic: "By that token a Zhu will rule in time to come—Heaven has given warning."

sentences.zh: 且木之數三，其禎也應在三紀之內乎！

translations.literal: Moreover wood's number is three—perhaps the blessing manifests within three reign periods!
translations.idiomatic: "And wood's number is three—perhaps the omen will run its course within three reigns!"

sentences.zh: 」鐸聞之，不復有言。

translations.literal: Duo heard this and spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: Duo heard him out and said nothing further.

sentences.zh: 天后朝有讖辭云：「首尾三鱗六十年，兩角犢子自狂顛，龍蛇相鬥血成川。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's reign a prophecy said: "Head and tail, three scales, sixty years; the two-horned calf goes mad by itself; dragons and snakes fight until the rivers run with blood."
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Empress Wu a prophecy ran: "Head and tail, three scales, sixty years; the two-horned calf runs wild; dragons and serpents battle until rivers run red."

sentences.zh: 」當時好事者解云：「兩角犢子，牛也，必有牛姓干唐祚。

translations.literal: At the time enthusiasts interpreted: "Two-horned calf—that is niu (ox); surely one surnamed Niu will undermine Tang's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries read it thus: "A two-horned calf is an ox—surely someone surnamed Niu will overturn Tang's mandate."

sentences.zh: 」故周子諒彈牛仙客，李德裕謗牛僧孺，皆以應圖讖為辭。

translations.literal: Hence Zhou Ziliang impeached Niu Senke, and Li Deyu slandered Niu Sengru, all citing fulfillment of the prophecy as their argument.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Zhou Ziliang attacked Niu Senke and Li Deyu vilified Niu Sengru—each invoking the prophecy as proof.

sentences.zh: 然「朱」字「牛」下安「八」，八即角之象也，故朱滔、朱泚構喪亂之禍，冀無妄之福，豈知應之帝也。

translations.literal: But the character Zhu has "ba" (eight) beneath "niu"—eight is the image of horn—so Zhu Tao and Zhu Ci brought calamity of disorder hoping for undeserved fortune, little knowing it foretold the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the character Zhu the element for "ox" stands above "eight"—eight being the sign of horns—so Zhu Tao and Zhu Ci stirred rebellion hoping for a throne that was not theirs, never guessing the omen pointed to the Emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 四月，唐帝御劄敕宰臣張文蔚等備法駕奉迎梁朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the Tang emperor issued an imperial decree commanding Zhang Wenwei and other chief ministers to prepare the imperial carriage to welcome the Liang court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Tang emperor sent an imperial decree ordering Zhang Wenwei and the other chief ministers to ready the imperial escort to receive the Liang.

sentences.zh: 宋州刺史王皋進赤烏一雙。

translations.literal: Wang Gao, prefect of Songzhou, presented a pair of red crows.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao, prefect of Songzhou, offered a pair of crimson crows.

sentences.zh: 又，宰臣張文蔚正押傳國寶、玉冊、金寶及文武群官、諸司儀仗法物及金吾左右二軍離鄭州。

translations.literal: Also, chief minister Zhang Wenwei personally escorted the dynastic seal, jade registers, gold seals, civil and military officials of all ranks, ritual regalia of every office, and the Left and Right Jinwu Armies as they departed Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Zhang Wenwei meanwhile led the imperial seal, jade books, gold regalia, the full civil and military establishment, ceremonial equipage of every bureau, and the Left and Right Jinwu guards out of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，達上源驛。

translations.literal: On bingchen they reached Shangyuan Post.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen they arrived at Shangyuan Post.

sentences.zh: 是日，慶雲見。

translations.literal: That day, auspicious clouds appeared.
translations.idiomatic: That day auspicious clouds were seen.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「王者創業興邦，立名傳世，必難知而示訓，從易避以便人。

translations.literal: An edict said: "When kings found states and establish names to pass down through generations, they must make what is hard to know into teaching and choose what is easy to avoid for the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Founders of dynasties who wish their names to endure must turn what is obscure into instruction and choose what is easy for the people to observe.

sentences.zh: 〈案：此下有闕文。〉

translations.literal: 〈Note: Text is missing here.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note: Text is missing here.〉

sentences.zh: 或稽其符命，應彼開基之義，垂諸象德之言。

translations.literal: Or they examine mandate tokens and respond to the meaning of founding a base, leaving words that embody symbolic virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Some consult portents that match the moment of founding, or phrases that embody the virtue of their emblem."

sentences.zh: 爰考簡書，求於往代，周王昌、發之號，漢帝詢、衍之文，或從一德以徽稱，或為二名而更易。

translations.literal: Examining brief histories and seeking examples from past ages—the styles of King Chang and King Fa of Zhou, the inscriptions of Emperors Xun and Yan of Han—some took a single virtue as their emblem, others changed because they had two personal names.
translations.idiomatic: Looking to the records of old: Zhou's Kings Chang and Fa, Han's Emperors Xun and Yan—some took one virtue as a style, others changed names because they bore two characters.

sentences.zh: 先王令典，布在縑緗。

translations.literal: The former kings' ordinances are set down in silk books.
translations.idiomatic: The precedents of former kings stand written in the classics.

sentences.zh: 寡人本名，兼於二字，且異帝王之號，仍兼易之難，郡職縣官，多須改換。

translations.literal: My original name combines two characters, differs from imperial styles, and still entails the difficulty of change—prefectural, circuit, and county offices would mostly need renaming.
translations.idiomatic: My birth name has two characters, unlike an emperor's style, and would be awkward to taboo—countless prefectural and county posts would need revision.

sentences.zh: 況宗廟不遷之業，憲章百世之規，事葉典儀，豈憚革易。

translations.literal: Moreover the enterprise of an undisturbed ancestral temple and institutions meant to last a hundred generations accord with canonical rites—how could one shrink from change?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ancestral rites and laws meant to last generations demand it—how could I refuse what ritual requires?

sentences.zh: 寡人今改名晃，是以天意雅符於明德，日光顯契于瑞文，昭融萬邦，理斯在是。

translations.literal: I now change my name to Huang—for thus Heaven's intent elegantly matches Bright Virtue, and sunlight clearly accords with auspicious script, illuminating ten thousand states; reason lies herein.
translations.idiomatic: I now take the name Huang—Heaven's will aligns with Bright Virtue, sunlight with the omen in writing, that all under heaven may be illumined; this is the fitting course.

sentences.zh: 庶順昊穹之意，永臻康濟之期。

translations.literal: May it accord with the Supreme Vault's intent and ever reach the season of peace and relief.
translations.idiomatic: May it satisfy Heaven above and bring lasting peace and plenty.

sentences.zh: 宜令有司分告天地宗廟，其舊名，中外章疏不得更有回避。

translations.literal: Let the relevant offices announce it in turn to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples; as for the old name, memorials within and without the court need no longer avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Let the proper offices report to Heaven, Earth, and the temples. The old name need no longer be tabooed in memorials at court or abroad.

sentences.zh: 」時將受禪，下教以本名二字異帝王之稱，故改名。

translations.literal: At the time he was about to receive the abdication; he issued this teaching because his original two-character name differed from an emperor's style—hence the change of name.
translations.idiomatic: He was on the verge of receiving the mandate; this edict explained that his two-character birth name was unsuitable for an emperor—hence the change.

sentences.zh: 己未，賜文武百官一百六十人本色衣一副。

translations.literal: On jiwei he bestowed one set of plain-color robes each upon one hundred sixty civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei he gave one set of plain court robes apiece to one hundred sixty officials, civil and military.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，即位。

translations.literal: On wuchen he ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen he took the throne.

sentences.zh: 制曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: His inaugural edict read:

sentences.zh: 王者受命於天，光宅四海，祗事上帝，寵綏下民。

translations.literal: The king receives the mandate from Heaven, dwells in glory over the four seas, reverently serves the Supreme Lord, and cherishes and pacifies the people below.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler receives Heaven's mandate, holds the realm in light, serves the Lord on High, and shelters the people below.

sentences.zh: 革故鼎新，諒歷數而先定，創業垂統，知圖籙以無差。

translations.literal: Renewing the old and establishing the new—surely the sequence of fate was fixed beforehand; founding the enterprise and handing down the succession—knowing the charts and registers are without error.
translations.idiomatic: To renew what is old and raise what is new—the turn of fortune was already settled; to found a line and pass it on—the portents left no doubt.

sentences.zh: 神器所歸，祥符合應。

translations.literal: Where the sacred vessel returns, auspicious tokens answer in accord.
translations.idiomatic: Where the sacred vessel belongs, omens align.

sentences.zh: 是以三正互用，五運相生，前朝道消，中原政散，瞻烏莫定，失鹿難追。

translations.literal: Thus the three orthodoxies alternate in use and the five phases generate one another; the former dynasty's Way waned and government in the Central Plain dissolved—like crows on the wing, none could settle; like the deer lost, none could recover it.
translations.idiomatic: The three calendars succeed one another; the five phases give birth in turn. Tang's Way faded and the heartland fell apart—no perch for the ravens, no catching the lost deer.

sentences.zh: 朕經緯風雷，沐浴霜露，四征七伐，垂三十年，糾合齊盟，翼戴唐室。

translations.literal: I have woven wind and thunder, bathed in frost and dew, campaigned in four directions and seven punitive expeditions for nearly thirty years, rallied allied states, and supported the House of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: I have braved storm and frost, fought east, west, north, and south for nearly thirty years, knit alliances together, and upheld the Tang house.

sentences.zh: 隨山刊木，罔憚胼胝；

translations.literal: Following mountains to hew wood, I did not shrink from calloused hands;
translations.idiomatic: I felled forests and opened roads without flinching from toil;

sentences.zh: 投袂揮戈，不遑寢處。

translations.literal: throwing up my sleeves to wield the spear, I had no leisure to lie down.
translations.idiomatic: I took up arms and scarcely slept.

sentences.zh: 洎上穹之所贊，知廣運之不興，莫諧輔漢之謀，徒罄事殷之禮。

translations.literal: When Heaven above came to aid, I knew the broad mandate would not revive; no harmony could be found in the plan to assist Han, and the rites of serving Yin were exhausted in vain.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven favored me I saw that the great mandate would not return to Tang; plans to prop up Han came to nothing, and the rites owed a fallen house were spent in vain.

sentences.zh: 唐主知英華已竭，算祀有終，釋龜鼎以如遺，推劍紱而相授。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler knew that splendor was spent and his allotted span had ended; he released the tortoise and tripod as a legacy and pushed sword and seal cord forward to confer them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang sovereign knew his glory was spent and his years were up; he set aside the regalia of empire and offered sword and seal.

sentences.zh: 朕懼德弗嗣，執謙允恭，避駿命于南河，眷清風于穎水。

translations.literal: I feared my virtue could not succeed and held to humility and deference, avoiding the august mandate at South River and cherishing the clear wind at Ying Stream.
translations.idiomatic: I feared I lacked the virtue to succeed and clung to humility, declining the throne at South River and longing for the ease of Ying Stream.

sentences.zh: 而乃列嶽群後，盈廷庶官，東西南北之人，斑白緇黃之眾，謂朕功蓋上下，澤被幽深，宜應天以順時，俾化家而為國。

translations.literal: Yet the peaks in rank and the hosts of officials, people from east, west, south, and north, and the multitude in plain cloth and monastic garb said my merit covered above and below and my grace reached the depths; I should respond to Heaven and accord with the season, transforming the family into a state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the lords of the mountains, the officials who filled the court, folk from every quarter, gray heads and monks alike, said my merit reached heaven and earth and my grace the depths—that I must answer Heaven, follow the season, and turn a house into a realm.

sentences.zh: 拒彼億兆，至於再三。

translations.literal: I refused those hundred millions, even to a third time.
translations.idiomatic: I refused the countless pleas, again and again.

sentences.zh: 且曰七政已齊，萬幾難曠。

translations.literal: They said moreover that the seven regulators were aligned and the myriad affairs could not be left vacant.
translations.idiomatic: They said the seven luminaries were in order and the myriad duties could not lie idle.

sentences.zh: 勉遵令典，爰正鴻名，告天地神祗，建宗廟社稷。

translations.literal: Reluctantly following the established canon, I now rectify the great name, announce it to the spirits of Heaven and Earth, and establish ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yielding at last to precedent, I set the great name, reported to Heaven and Earth and the spirits, and founded temples and altars.

sentences.zh: 顧惟涼德，曷副樂推，栗若履冰，懍如馭朽。

translations.literal: Looking back on my meager virtue, how can I match what joy has pushed forward? I tremble as if treading on ice, I am wary as if driving rotten wood.
translations.idiomatic: My virtue is slight beside what men have urged upon me; I tremble as on thin ice, I drive as over rotten timber.

sentences.zh: 金行啟祚，玉曆建元，方宏經治之規，宜布惟新之令。

translations.literal: The Metal phase begins its fortune; the jade calendar establishes a new origin—now is the time to enlarge the rules of governance and proclaim orders of renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Metal begins its reign; the calendar starts anew—it is time to widen governance and proclaim a fresh order.

sentences.zh: 可改唐天祐四年為開平元年，國號大樑。

translations.literal: Let the fourth year of Tang's Tianyou be changed to the first year of Kaiping; the state name is Great Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Let Tang's Tianyou year 4 become Kaiping year 1; the realm shall be called Great Liang.

sentences.zh: 《書》載虞賓，斯為令範，《詩》稱周客，蓋有明文。

translations.literal: The 《Book》 records the guest of Yu as a fine model; the 《Odes》 praise the guest of Zhou—there is clear text for this.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Book of Documents》 praises Yu's guest as the model; the 《Classic of Poetry》 honors Zhou's guest—text enough for what follows.

sentences.zh: 是用先封，以禮後嗣，宜以曹州濟陰之邑奉唐主，封為濟陰王。

translations.literal: Therefore we first enfeoff and only afterward install the successor: let the seat of Jiyin in Caozhou support the Tang ruler, enfeoffing him as Prince of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: So we enfeoff before we enthrone: Caozhou's Jiyin district shall sustain the Tang ruler as Prince of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 凡曰軌儀，並遵故實。

translations.literal: All ceremonial norms shall follow former practice.
translations.idiomatic: Every rite shall follow established usage.

sentences.zh: 姬庭多士，比是殷臣；

translations.literal: Many officers of the Zhou court were likewise ministers of Yin;
translations.idiomatic: Men of the Zhou court served Yin as well;

sentences.zh: 楚國群材，終為晉用。

translations.literal: talents of the state of Chu in the end were used by Jin.
translations.idiomatic: and Chu's worthies ended in Jin's employ.

sentences.zh: 歷觀前載，自有通規，但遵故事之文，勿替在公之效。

translations.literal: Reviewing former records, there has always been a common rule—only follow the language of old stories and do not diminish the effect of serving in office.
translations.idiomatic: History offers a constant rule: follow precedent and do not lessen the duty of public service.

sentences.zh: 應是唐朝中外文武舊臣，見任前資官爵，一切仍舊。

translations.literal: All former civil and military officials of Tang, whether currently serving or holding prior ranks and titles, shall remain as before in every respect.
translations.idiomatic: Every Tang official, civil or military, in post or holding former rank, keeps office and title unchanged.

sentences.zh: 凡百有位，無易厥章，陳力濟時，盡瘁事我。

translations.literal: For the hundred ranks, let none change their statutes; exert your strength to aid the age and exhaust yourselves in serving me.
translations.idiomatic: Let none among the hundred offices alter his charge; serve the times with all your strength and give your utmost to me.

sentences.zh: 古者興王之地，受命之邦，集大勳有異庶方，沾慶澤所宜加等。

translations.literal: In antiquity the place where a king rose and the state that received the mandate, having gathered great merit unlike other regions, deserved added favor when blessings were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Anciently the land that raised a king and the state that received the mandate, for uncommon merit, deserved extra grace when rewards were given.

sentences.zh: 故豐沛著啟祚之美，穰鄧有建都之榮，用壯鴻基，且旌故里，爰遵令典，先示殊恩。

translations.literal: Thus Feng and Pei showed the beauty of founding fortune, Rang and Deng the glory of establishing the capital—strengthening the great foundation and honoring the old home, following the established canon, we first display special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Feng and Pei shone as seats of founding; Rang and Deng as places of enthronement—so we honor the cradle of empire and, by ancient right, show favor first to our home.

sentences.zh: 宜升汴州為開封府，建名東都。

translations.literal: Bianzhou should be promoted to Kaifeng Prefecture and styled the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Bianzhou is raised to Kaifeng Prefecture and named the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 其東都改為西都，仍廢京兆府為雍州佑國軍節度使。

translations.literal: The former Eastern Capital is changed to the Western Capital, and Jingzhao Prefecture is abolished in favor of a Youzhou Youguo Army military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The old Eastern Capital becomes the Western Capital; Jingzhao Prefecture is abolished and Youzhou given a Youguo Army governor.

sentences.zh: 〈《五代會要》：「四月，改京兆府為大安府，長安縣為大安縣，萬年縣為大年縣，仍置佑國軍節度使額。

translations.literal: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: "In the fourth month Jingzhao Prefecture was changed to Da'an Prefecture, Chang'an County to Da'an County, Wannian County to Danian County, and the Youguo Army governorship was established.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records: "In the fourth month Jingzhao became Da'an Prefecture, Chang'an county Da'an, Wannian county Danian, and the Youguo Army post was created.

sentences.zh: 始命韓建為佑國軍節度使。」〉

translations.literal: Han Jian was first appointed military governor of the Youguo Army."〉
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian was first named Youguo Army governor."〉

sentences.zh: 是日大酺，賞賜有差。

translations.literal: That day there was a great communal feast; rewards were graded.
translations.idiomatic: That day the court held a grand feast; gifts varied by rank.

sentences.zh: 《通鑒》：甲辰，唐昭宣帝降御劄禪位於梁。

translations.literal: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: On jiachen, Tang's Emperor Zhaoxuan issued an imperial decree abdicating the throne to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 notes: On jiachen Emperor Zhaoxuan of Tang issued an imperial decree abdicating to Liang.

sentences.zh: 以攝中書令張文蔚為冊禮使，禮部尚書蘇循副之；

translations.literal: Acting Zhongshu Ling Zhang Wenwei was made chief of the enfeoffment rites, with Minister of Rites Su Xun as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Acting Zhongshu Ling Zhang Wenwei was made chief envoy for the investiture, with Minister of Rites Su Xun as deputy;

sentences.zh: 攝侍中楊涉為押傳國寶使，翰林院學士張策副之；

translations.literal: Acting Shizhong Yang She was made chief custodian of the dynastic seal, with Hanlin Academician Zhang Ce as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Acting Shizhong Yang She was made chief custodian of the imperial seal, with Hanlin Academician Zhang Ce as deputy;

sentences.zh: 御史大夫薛貽矩為押金寶使，尚書左丞趙光逢副之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju was made chief custodian of the gold regalia, with Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat Zhao Guangfeng as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju was made chief custodian of the gold regalia, with Left Assistant Minister Zhao Guangfeng as deputy.

sentences.zh: 帥百官備法駕，詣大樑。

translations.literal: They led the hundred officials with the imperial carriage to Great Liang.
translations.idiomatic: They led the full court with the imperial escort to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 甲子，張文蔚、楊涉乘輅自上源驛至，從冊寶諸司各備儀衛鹵簿前導，百官從其後，至金祥殿前陳之。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Zhang Wenwei and Yang She rode the imperial carriage from Shangyuan Post; the offices bearing registers and seals each prepared guards and insignia to go before, the hundred officials following behind, until they arrayed them before the Hall of Golden Auspice.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Zhang Wenwei and Yang She came in the imperial carriage from Shangyuan Post, regalia and seals borne ahead with full guard, officials following, and arrayed all before the Hall of Golden Auspice.

sentences.zh: 王被袞冕，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: The king donned the imperial robes and took the emperor's seat.
translations.idiomatic: He assumed the imperial regalia and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 張文蔚、蘇循奉冊升殿進讀，楊涉、張策、薛貽矩、趙光逢以次奉寶升殿，讀已，降，帥百官舞蹈稱駕。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenwei and Su Xun bore the register up the hall and read it; Yang She, Zhang Ce, Xue Yiju, and Zhao Guangfeng in turn bore the seals up the hall; when the reading was done they descended and led the hundred officials in ritual dance and acclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenwei and Su Xun presented and read the register; Yang She, Zhang Ce, Xue Yiju, and Zhao Guangfeng presented the seals in turn; then they led the court in the bowing dance and acclamation.

sentences.zh: 帝遂與文蔚等宴於元德殿。

translations.literal: The Emperor then feasted with Wenwei and the others in the Hall of Primordial Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then banqueted Wenwei and the others in the Hall of Primordial Virtue.

sentences.zh: 帝舉酒曰：「朕輔政未久，此皆諸公推戴之力。

translations.literal: The Emperor raised his cup and said: "I have assisted in government only a short while; this is all the power of your pushing me forward."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor raised his wine and said: "I have governed but briefly—this is entirely your doing in elevating me."

sentences.zh: 」文蔚等慚懼，俯伏不能對，獨蘇循、薛貽矩及刑部尚書張禕盛稱帝功德，宜應天順人。

translations.literal: Wenwei and the others were ashamed and afraid, bowed prostrate and could not reply; only Su Xun, Xue Yiju, and Minister of Justice Zhang Yi lavishly praised the Emperor's merit and virtue, saying he should respond to Heaven and accord with the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei and the rest were abashed and speechless on their faces; only Su Xun, Xue Yiju, and Minister of Justice Zhang Yi loudly praised the Emperor's merit as fitting Heaven and the people.

sentences.zh: 宋州刺史王皋進兩岐麥，陳州袁象先進白兔一，付史館編錄，兼示百官。

translations.literal: Wang Gao, prefect of Songzhou, presented double-eared wheat; Yuan Xiangxian of Chenzhou presented one white hare—both were sent to the Historiography Office for record and shown to the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao of Songzhou offered double-eared wheat; Yuan Xiangxian of Chenzhou a white hare—both were recorded by the Historiography Office and displayed to the court.

sentences.zh: 詔在京司及諸軍州縣印一例鑄換，其篆文則各如舊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that seals of capital offices and of all army prefectures and counties be recast uniformly; the seal script should each remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered all seals of capital bureaus and of armies, prefectures, and counties recast at once, each keeping its former inscription.

sentences.zh: 辛未，武安軍節度使馬殷進封楚王。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Ma Yin, military governor of the Wu'an Army, was advanced and enfeoffed as King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Ma Yin, governor of the Wu'an Army, was advanced to King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 乙太府卿敬翔知崇政院，翔與帷幄之謀，故首擢焉。

translations.literal: On the day yi, Grand Master of Splendid Affairs Jing Xiang was appointed to oversee the Chongzhengyuan; Xiang had shared in secret planning within the tent, hence he was first promoted.
translations.idiomatic: On a yi day Grand Master of Splendid Affairs Jing Xiang was put in charge of the Chongzhengyuan—first among promotions because he had shared the Emperor's counsels in the field.

sentences.zh: 追尊四代廟號：高祖媯州府君上諡曰宣元皇帝，廟號肅祖，太廟第一室，陵號興極陵，祖妣高平縣君范氏追諡宣僖皇后；

translations.literal: Posthumous temple names for four generations were honored: the High Ancestor, Lord of Guizhou Prefecture, was given the posthumous title Emperor Xuanyuan, temple name Sizu, first chamber of the Great Temple, tomb name Xingji, and ancestress Lady Fan of Gaoping County was posthumously titled Empress Xuanxi;
translations.idiomatic: Four ancestral generations received temple names: the High Ancestor, Lord of Guizhou, posthumous Emperor Xuanyuan, temple Sizu, first chamber, tomb Xingji; Lady Fan of Gaoping, Empress Xuanxi;

sentences.zh: 皇曾祖宣惠王上諡曰光獻皇帝，廟號敬祖，第二室，陵號永安，祖妣秦國夫人楊氏追諡光孝皇后；

translations.literal: the Emperor's great-grandfather, King Xuanhui, was given the posthumous title Emperor Guangxian, temple name Jingzu, second chamber, tomb Yong'an, and ancestress Lady Yang of Qin was posthumously titled Empress Guangxiao;
translations.idiomatic: the great-grandfather, King Xuanhui, posthumous Emperor Guangxian, temple Jingzu, second chamber, tomb Yong'an; Lady Yang of Qin, Empress Guangxiao;

sentences.zh: 皇祖武元王上諡曰昭武皇帝，廟號憲祖，第三室，陵號光天，祖妣吳國夫人劉氏追諡昭懿皇后；

translations.literal: the Emperor's grandfather, King Wuyuan, was given the posthumous title Emperor Zhaowu, temple name Xianzu, third chamber, tomb name Guangtian, and ancestress Lady Liu of Wu was posthumously titled Empress Zhaoyi;
translations.idiomatic: the grandfather, King Wuyuan, posthumous Emperor Zhaowu, temple Xianzu, third chamber, tomb Guangtian; Lady Liu of Wu, Empress Zhaoyi;

sentences.zh: 皇考文明王上諡曰文穆皇帝，廟號烈祖，第四室，陵號咸寧，皇妣晉國太夫人王氏追諡文惠皇后。

translations.literal: the Emperor's father, King Wenming, was given the posthumous title Emperor Wenmu, temple name Liezu, fourth chamber, tomb Xianning, and the Emperor's mother, Grand Lady of Jin, Lady Wang, was posthumously titled Empress Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: the father, King Wenming, posthumous Emperor Wenmu, temple Liezu, fourth chamber, tomb Xianning; the mother, Grand Lady of Jin Wang, Empress Wenhui.

sentences.zh: 以宣武節度副使皇子友文為開封尹，判建昌院事。

translations.literal: The Prince Youwen, deputy military governor of Xuanwu and imperial son, was made Prefect of Kaifeng and given charge of Jianchang Court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Youwen, deputy Xuanwu governor and imperial son, was made Prefect of Kaifeng and superintendent of the Jianchang Court.

sentences.zh: 友文，本康氏子也，帝養以為子。

translations.literal: Youwen was originally a son of the Kang clan; the Emperor adopted and raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen was born to the Kang clan; the Emperor adopted him as his son.

sentences.zh: 是月，制宮殿門及都門名額：正殿為崇元殿，東殿為元德殿，內殿為金祥殿，萬歲堂為萬歲殿，門如殿名。

translations.literal: That month, names were fixed for palace gates and capital gates: the main hall was Chongyuan Hall, the eastern hall Primordial Virtue Hall, the inner hall Golden Auspice Hall, the Hall of Ten Thousand Years became Ten Thousand Years Hall, and gates took the names of their halls.
translations.idiomatic: That month palace and capital gates were named: main hall Chongyuan, east hall Primordial Virtue, inner hall Golden Auspice, Hall of Ten Thousand Years renamed Ten Thousand Years Hall—gates matching their halls.

sentences.zh: 帝自謂以金德王，又以福建上獻鸚鵡，諸州相繼上白烏、白兔洎白蓮之合蒂者，以為金行應運之兆，故名殿曰金祥。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered himself king by the virtue of Metal; moreover Fujian presented parrots, and prefectures in succession presented white crows, white hares, and white lotuses with conjoined stems, taking these as omens that the Metal phase answered the mandate—hence the hall was named Golden Auspice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held that he ruled by Metal's virtue; Fujian sent parrots, and one prefecture after another white crows, white hares, and twin-stemmed white lotuses—omens of Metal's mandate—so the hall was called Golden Auspice.

sentences.zh: 以大內正門為元化門，皇牆南門為建國門，滴漏門為啟運門，下馬門為升龍門，元德殿前門為崇明門，正殿東門為金烏門，西門為玉兔門，正衙東門為崇禮門，東偏門為銀台門，宴堂門為德陽門，天王門為賓天門，皇牆東門為寬仁門，浚儀門為厚載門，皇牆西門為神獸門，望京門為金鳳門，宋門為觀化門，尉氏門為高明門，鄭門為開明門，梁門為乾象門，酸棗門為興和門，封丘門為含耀門，曹門為建陽門。

translations.literal: The great inner main gate was made Primordial Transformation Gate; the southern gate of the imperial wall, Founding the State Gate; the clepsydra gate, Opening Fortune Gate; the dismounting gate, Ascending Dragon Gate; the front gate of the Primordial Virtue Hall, Honoring Clarity Gate; the main hall's east gate, Golden Crow Gate; west gate, Jade Rabbit Gate; the main court's east gate, Honoring Rites Gate; east side gate, Silver Terrace Gate; banquet hall gate, Virtue and Yang Gate; Heavenly King Gate, Guest of Heaven Gate; the imperial wall's east gate, Broad Benevolence Gate; Junyi Gate, Heavy Burden Gate; the imperial wall's west gate, Divine Beast Gate; Wangjing Gate, Golden Phoenix Gate; Song Gate, Observing Transformation Gate; Weishi Gate, Lofty Bright Gate; Zheng Gate, Opening Bright Gate; Liang Gate, Qian Symbol Gate; Suanzao Gate, Rising Harmony Gate; Fengqiu Gate, Containing Glory Gate; Cao Gate, Establishing Yang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The inner main gate became Primordial Transformation; the imperial south wall, Founding the State; the water-clock gate, Opening Fortune; the dismounting gate, Ascending Dragon; Primordial Virtue's front gate, Honoring Clarity; the main hall's east Golden Crow and west Jade Rabbit; the court's east Honoring Rites and east side Silver Terrace; the banquet hall Virtue and Yang; Heavenly King, Guest of Heaven; the wall's east Broad Benevolence; Junyi, Heavy Burden; west Divine Beast; Wangjing, Golden Phoenix; Song, Observing Transformation; Weishi, Lofty Bright; Zheng, Opening Bright; Liang, Qian Symbol; Suanzao, Rising Harmony; Fengqiu, Containing Glory; Cao, Establishing Yang.

sentences.zh: 升開封、浚儀為赤縣，尉氏、封丘、雍丘、陳留為畿縣。

translations.literal: Kaifeng and Junyi were promoted to chief counties; Weishi, Fengqiu, Yongqiu, and Chenliu became metropolitan counties.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng and Junyi were raised to chief counties; Weishi, Fengqiu, Yongqiu, and Chenliu to metropolitan counties.

sentences.zh: 〈《五代會要》：四月，改左右長直為左右龍虎軍，左右內衙為左右羽林軍，左右堅銳夾馬突將為左右神武軍，左右親隨軍將馬軍為左右龍驤軍。〉

translations.literal: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: In the fifth month the Left and Right Changzhi were changed to Left and Right Dragon-Tiger Armies, the Left and Right Inner Palace to Left and Right Forest of Plumes Armies, the Left and Right Sharp Lances and Horse-chargers to Left and Right Divine Martial Armies, and the Left and Right Personal Followers and Horse Generals to Left and Right Dragon-Prancing Armies.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records: In the fifth month the Left and Right Changzhi became Dragon-Tiger Armies, the inner guards Forest of Plumes Armies, the sharp lancers and chargers Divine Martial Armies, and the personal horse guards Dragon-Prancing Armies.〉

sentences.zh: 五月，以唐朝宰臣張文蔚、楊涉並為門下侍郎、平章事；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;

sentences.zh: 以御史大夫薛貽矩為中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 帝初受禪，求理尤切，委宰臣搜訪賢良。

translations.literal: When the Emperor first received the mandate, he sought good government with especial urgency and entrusted the chief ministers to search out the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh on the throne, the Emperor was urgent for good rule and charged his chief ministers to seek out talent.

sentences.zh: 或有在下位抱負器業久不得伸者，特加擢用；

translations.literal: If there were those in low position who harbored ability and long could not advance, they were specially promoted;
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent in humble posts who had waited too long were promoted outright;

sentences.zh: 有明政理得失之道規救時病者，可陳章疏，當親鑒擇利害施行，然後賞以爵秩；

translations.literal: if there were those who understood the gains and losses of government and had plans to remedy the ills of the age, they might submit memorials—the Emperor would personally examine and choose what was harmful or beneficial to implement, and only then reward with rank;
translations.idiomatic: those who saw what was right or wrong in policy and offered remedies could memorialise—the Emperor would read and adopt what helped or hurt, then grant rank;

sentences.zh: 有晦跡丘園不求聞達者，令彼長吏備禮邀致，冀無遺逸之恨。

translations.literal: if there were those who hid their traces in hills and gardens and did not seek renown, let their local superiors with full rites invite them to come, hoping there would be no regret for those overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: recluses who sought no fame were to be invited with full ceremony by their magistrates, lest any worthy be missed.

sentences.zh: 進封河南尹兼河陽節度使張全義為魏王，兩浙節度使錢鏐進封吳越王。

translations.literal: Zhang Quanyi, Prince of Wei and Henan Prefect concurrently military governor of Heyang, was advanced in enfeoffment; Qian Liu, military governor of the two Zhe circuits, was advanced and enfeoffed as King of Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyi of Henan and Heyang was raised to Prince of Wei; Qian Liu of the two Zhes to King of Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，有司奏，以降誕之日為大明節，休假前後各一日。

translations.literal: On xinsi the relevant offices memorialized that the day of the imperial birthday be styled the Great Brightness Festival, with leave one day before and after.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the ministries proposed the imperial birthday as the Great Brightness Festival, with a holiday on either side.

sentences.zh: 壬午，保義軍節度使朱友謙進百官衣二百副。

translations.literal: On renwu, Zhu Youqian, military governor of the Baoyi Army, presented two hundred sets of official robes.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Zhu Youqian of the Baoyi Army offered two hundred sets of court robes.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，立皇兄全昱為廣王，皇子友文為博王，友珪為郢王，友璋為福王，友雍為賀王，友徽為建王。

translations.literal: On xinmao the Emperor's elder brother Quanyu was established as Prince of Guang, the imperial son Youwen as Prince of Bo, Yougui as Prince of E, Youzhang as Prince of Fu, Youyong as Prince of He, and Youhui as Prince of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the Emperor enfeoffed his brother Quanyu as Prince of Guang and his sons Youwen, Yougui, Youzhang, Youyong, and Youhui as Princes of Bo, E, Fu, He, and Jian.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以東都舊第為建昌宮，改判建昌院事為建昌宮使。

translations.literal: On jiawu the former Eastern Capital residence was made Jianchang Palace, and the post of superintendent of Jianchang Court affairs was changed to superintendent of Jianchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the old Eastern Capital residence became Jianchang Palace, and the Jianchang Court superintendent became palace superintendent.

sentences.zh: 初，帝創業之時，以四鎮兵馬倉庫籍繁，因總置建昌院以領之，至是改為宮，蓋重其事也。

translations.literal: At first, when the Emperor was founding the enterprise, because the registers of troops, horses, and storehouses of the four circuits were numerous, he gathered them under the Jianchang Court to administer them; now it was changed to a palace, showing the weight attached to the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In founding days the four circuits' troop, horse, and granary rolls had been centralized in the Jianchang Court; elevating it to a palace marked how seriously he took the office.

sentences.zh: 甲午，詔天下管屬及州縣官名犯廟諱者，各宜改換：城門郎改為門局郎，茂州改為汶州，桂州慕化縣改為歸化縣，潘州茂名縣改為越裳縣。

translations.literal: On jiawu an edict ordered that wherever official titles in the realm and in prefectures and counties violated temple taboo, each should be changed: chengmenglang to gate-bureau lang, Maozhou to Wenzhou, Guizhou's Muhua County to Guihua County, Panzhou's Maoming County to Yueshang County.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu an edict ordered titles that clashed with imperial taboo renamed everywhere—chengmenglang to gate-bureau lang, Maozhou to Wenzhou, Muhua to Guihua, Maoming to Yueshang.

sentences.zh: 魏泰《東軒筆錄》：京師呼城外為州東、州西、州南、州北，而韋城、相城、胙城等縣，但呼韋縣、相縣、胙縣，蓋沿梁時避諱之舊也。

translations.literal: Wei Tai's 《Eastern Study Notes》 says: The capital called outside the walls "east of the prefecture," "west of the prefecture," and so on, while Weicheng, Xiangcheng, Zuocheng, and other counties were simply called Wei County, Xiang County, Zuo County—continuing the old practice of avoiding taboo from Liang times.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Tai's 《Eastern Study Notes》 notes that the capital spoke of "east of the prefecture" and the like, while Weicheng and similar counties were shortened to Wei County—custom carried over from Liang taboo.

sentences.zh: 詔樞密院宜改為崇政院，以知院事敬翔為院使。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that the Bureau of Military Affairs be changed to the Chongzhengyuan, with Jing Xiang, who knew its affairs, as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs became the Chongzhengyuan, with Jing Xiang as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 改文思院為乾文院，同和院改為佐鸞院。

translations.literal: The Wensi Court was changed to the Qianwen Court, and the Tonghe Court to the Zuoluan Court.
translations.idiomatic: The Wensi Court became Qianwen; the Tonghe Court, Zuoluan.

sentences.zh: 〈《五代會要》：五月，改御食使為司膳使，小馬坊使為天驥使。

translations.literal: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: In the fifth month the imperial-food commissioner was changed to palace-provisions commissioner, and the small horse-park commissioner to heaven-steed commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records: In the fifth month the imperial-food office became palace provisions, the small horse park the heaven-steed office.

sentences.zh: 以西都水北宅為大昌宮，廢雍州太清宮，改西都太微宮，亳州太清宮皆為觀，諸州紫極宮皆為老君廟。

translations.literal: The Western Capital's Shuibei residence was made Dachang Palace; Yongzhou's Grand Supreme Unity Palace was abolished; the Western Capital's Grand Microcosm Palace and Bozhou's Grand Supreme Unity Palace were all changed to abbeys; Purple Ultimate Palaces in all prefectures were changed to Lord Lao temples.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Capital's north-of-the-water residence became Dachang Palace; Yongzhou's Supreme Unity Abbey was abolished; western and Bozhou Supreme Unity sites became abbeys; every prefecture's Purple Ultimate Palace became a Lord Lao temple.

sentences.zh: 泉州僧智宣自西域回，進辟支佛骨及梵夾經律。

translations.literal: The monk Zhixuan of Quanzhou returned from the Western Regions and presented pratyeka-buddha relics and Sanskrit sutras of discipline and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixuan, a monk of Quanzhou, returned from the Western Regions with pratyeka-buddha relics and Sanskrit scriptures of vinaya and doctrine.

sentences.zh: 丙申，御元德殿，宴犒諸軍使劉捍、符道昭已下，賜物有差。〉

translations.literal: On bingchen the Emperor held court in the Hall of Primordial Virtue, feasted and rewarded army commissioners from Liu Han and Fu Daozhao down, bestowing goods in graded amounts.〉
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen he held court in the Hall of Primordial Virtue and feasted army commissioners from Liu Han and Fu Daozhao downward, with graded gifts.〉

sentences.zh: 是月，青州、許州、定州三鎮節度使請開內宴，各賜方物。

translations.literal: That month the military governors of Qingzhou, Xuzhou, and Dingzhou requested inner banquets; each was granted local products.
translations.idiomatic: That month the governors of Qing, Xu, and Ding asked for palace banquets and received local tribute in return.

sentences.zh: 以青州節度使韓建守司徒、平章事。

translations.literal: Han Jian, military governor of Qingzhou, was appointed Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian of Qingzhou was made Minister of Works and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 帝以建有文武材，且詳於稼穡利害、軍旅之事、籌度經費，欲盡詢焉，恩澤特異于時，罕有比者；

translations.literal: The Emperor considered Jian to have civil and military talent and to be well versed in the harm and benefit of farming, military affairs, and calculating expenses; wishing to inquire fully, his favor at the time was rarely matched;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor valued Jian for civil and military gifts and for knowing farming, war, and budgets inside out—his favor was almost unmatched—

sentences.zh: 隨拜為上相，賜賚甚厚。

translations.literal: he was soon appointed chief minister, with very rich gifts.
translations.idiomatic: and soon made chief minister with lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 宿州刺史王儒進白兔一，濮州刺史圖嘉禾瑞麥以進。

translations.literal: Wang Ru, prefect of Suzhou, presented one white hare; the prefect of Pu presented a diagram of auspicious grain and lucky wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru of Suzhou sent a white hare; the Pu prefect a chart of auspicious grain and lucky wheat.

sentences.zh: 廣州進奇寶名藥，品類甚多。

translations.literal: Guangzhou presented rare treasures and famous medicines in very many kinds.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou sent rare treasures and famed drugs in great variety.

sentences.zh: 河南尹張全義進開平元年已前羨余錢十萬貫、綢六千匹、綿三十萬兩，仍請每年上供定額每歲貢絹三萬匹，以為常式。

translations.literal: Zhang Quanyi, Henan Prefect, presented surplus money of one hundred thousand strings from before Kaiping year 1, six thousand bolts of silk, and three hundred thousand taels of cotton, and further requested a fixed annual tribute of thirty thousand bolts of silk as a standing rule.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyi of Henan offered a hundred thousand strings of surplus coin from before Kaiping 1, six thousand bolts of silk, and three hundred thousand taels of cotton, and asked that thirty thousand bolts of silk yearly be fixed as tribute.

sentences.zh: 荊南高季昌進瑞橘數十顆，質狀百味，倍勝常貢。

translations.literal: Gao Jichang of Jingnan presented several tens of auspicious oranges, their quality and form a hundredfold better than ordinary tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jichang of Jingnan sent dozens of auspicious oranges, finer in taste and look than ordinary tribute by far.

sentences.zh: 且橘當冬熟，今方仲夏，時人咸異其事，因稱為瑞。

translations.literal: Oranges should ripen in winter; now it was midsummer—people of the time all marveled at the matter and therefore called them auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Oranges ripen in winter, yet it was midsummer—men took it for a miracle and called them auspicious.

sentences.zh: 六月，幸乾元院，宴召宰臣、學士及諸道入貢陪臣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Emperor visited the Qianyuan Court and banqueted chief ministers, academicians, and tribute envoys from the circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he visited the Qianyuan Court and feasted chief ministers, Hanlin scholars, and circuit envoys.

sentences.zh: 己亥，帝御崇元殿，內出追尊四廟上諡號玉冊寶共八副，宰臣文武百官儀仗鼓吹導引至太廟行事。

translations.literal: On jihai the Emperor held court in the Hall of Chongyuan, brought out from within the eight jade registers and seals of posthumous titles for the four temples, and with chief ministers, civil and military officials, guards, and musicians as escort proceeded to the Great Temple to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he held court in Chongyuan Hall, produced eight jade books and seals of posthumous honor for the four temples, and with full court and guard went to the Great Temple to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，司天監奏：「日辰內有『戊』字，請改為『武』。

translations.literal: On guimao the Directorate of Astronomy memorialized: "Within the day-cycle there is the character 'wu'; please change it to 'wu' (martial)."
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the Directorate of Astronomy reported: "The day-cycle contains the character wu—we ask it be changed to wu, 'martial.'"

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，詔以前朝官僚，譴逐南荒，積年未經昭雪，其間有懷抱材器為時所嫉者，深負冤抑。

translations.literal: On guihai an edict said: "Former dynasty officials banished to the southern wilds, for years not yet cleared—among them are those of embraced talent whom the age envied, deeply wronged and suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai an edict said: "Tang officials exiled south, uncleared for years, include men of talent wronged by their times.

sentences.zh: 仍令錄其名姓，盡復官資，兼告諭諸道令津致赴闕。

translations.literal: Let their names be recorded, offices and salaries fully restored, and proclamations sent to every circuit to ferry them to court.
translations.idiomatic: Record their names, restore rank and pay, and tell every circuit to bring them to court."

sentences.zh: 如已亡歿，並許歸葬，以明恩蕩。

translations.literal: If they had already died, burial was permitted, to show the breadth of grace.
translations.idiomatic: Those already dead might be buried at home—a sign of mercy."

sentences.zh: 以西都徽安門北路逼近大內宮垣，兼非民便，令移自榆林直趨端門之南。

translations.literal: The road north of the Western Capital's Huian Gate lay close to the inner palace wall and was not convenient for the people; it was ordered moved from Yulin straight to the south of the Duan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The road north of the Western Capital's Huian Gate hugged the palace wall and troubled the people; it was shifted from Yulin to south of the Duan Gate.

sentences.zh: 改耀州報恩禪院為興國寺。

translations.literal: Yaozhou's Baoen Chan Monastery was changed to Xingguo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yaozhou's Baoen Chan Monastery became Xingguo Temple.

sentences.zh: 馬殷奏破淮寇；

translations.literal: Ma Yin memorialized that he had broken the Huai bandits;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin reported victory over Huai raiders;

sentences.zh: 靜海軍節度使曲裕卒。

translations.literal: Qu Yu, military governor of the Jinghai Army, died.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yu, governor of the Jinghai Army, died.

sentences.zh: 七月丙申，以靜海軍行營司馬權知留後曲顥起復為安南都護，充節度使。

translations.literal: On bingchen of the seventh month Qu Hao, acting Jinghai Army campaign staff officer and acting regional inspector, was recalled from mourning to be Protector-General of Annan and full military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen in the seventh month Qu Hao, acting Jinghai staff officer and acting inspector, was recalled from mourning as Protector-General of Annan and full governor.

sentences.zh: 〈《五代會要》：七月，敕云：「建國遷都，俾新其制，況山河之險，表裏為防。

translations.literal: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: In the seventh month an edict said: "Founding the state and moving the capital require new institutions; moreover the strategic passes, inner and outer, are our defense.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records: In the seventh month an edict said: "With the capital moved east, defenses must be renewed.

sentences.zh: 今二京俱在關東以內，仍以潼關隸陝州，復置河潼軍使，命虢州刺史兼領之。」〉

translations.literal: Now both capitals lie within the pass eastward; still let Tong Pass belong to Shaanzhou, restore the He-Tong Army commissioner, and command the prefect of Guo to hold the post concurrently."〉
translations.idiomatic: Both capitals now lie east of the pass; Tong Pass goes to Shaanzhou, the He-Tong Army post is restored, and the Guo prefect shall hold it."〉

sentences.zh: 其月，敕改虎牢關為軍，仍置虎牢關軍使。

translations.literal: That month an edict changed Hulao Pass to an army and established a Hulao Pass army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That month Hulao Pass was made an army command with its own commissioner.

sentences.zh: 己亥，追尊皇妣為皇太后。

translations.literal: On jihai the Emperor's mother was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the Emperor's mother was posthumously titled Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 八月，以潞州軍前屯師旅，壁壘未收，乃別議戎帥，於是以亳州刺史李思安充潞州行營都統。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, because the army before Luzhou was encamped and the ramparts not yet taken, another commander was chosen; Li Si'an, prefect of Bozhou, was made overall commander of the Luzhou campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, with Luzhou still besieged, a new commander was named: Li Si'an of Bozhou, overall chief of the Luzhou campaign.

sentences.zh: 敕：「朝廷之儀，封冊為重，用報勳烈，以隆恩榮，固合親臨，式光典禮。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Court ceremony and enfeoffment are weighty—they repay merit and magnify favor; it is fitting that the sovereign attend in person and glorify the canon.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Court ritual and investiture are grave—they reward merit and magnify grace; the sovereign should attend in person.

sentences.zh: 舊章久缺，自我復行。

translations.literal: The old statutes long lacked this; from me it is revived.
translations.idiomatic: The old rule had lapsed; I restore it.

sentences.zh: 今後每封冊大臣，宜令有司備臨軒之禮。」

translations.literal: Hereafter, whenever a great minister is enfeoffed, the relevant offices should prepare the rite of audience at the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whenever a great minister is enfeoffed, the proper offices shall prepare the throne-side rite."

sentences.zh: 〈《五代會要》：八月，敕云：「諸道所有軍事申奏，令直至右銀台門，委客省使畫時引進，尋常公事依前四方館收接。」〉

translations.literal: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: In the eighth month an edict said: "Military memorials from every circuit shall go directly to the Right Silver Terrace Gate; the guest-reception commissioner shall present them at once; routine business continues through the Four Directions Hall."〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records: In the eighth month an edict said: "Circuit military memorials go straight to the Right Silver Terrace Gate for immediate presentation; routine business still through the Four Directions Hall."〉

sentences.zh: 甲子平明前，老人星見於南極。

translations.literal: Before dawn on jiazi the Old Man Star appeared at the south pole.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn on jiazi the Old Man Star appeared at the southern pole.

sentences.zh: 壬申，密州進嘉禾，又有合歡榆樹，並圖形以獻。

translations.literal: On renshen Mizhou presented auspicious grain, and also an interlocking-locust tree; both were diagrammed and presented.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Mizhou sent auspicious grain and an interlocking-locust tree, both drawn and presented.

sentences.zh: 是月，隰州奏，大寧縣至固鎮上下二百里，今月八日，黃河清，至十月如故。

translations.literal: That month Xizhou reported that from Daning County to Gu Town, two hundred li up and down, on the eighth day of the month the Yellow River ran clear, remaining so until the tenth month as before.
translations.idiomatic: That month Xizhou reported that for two hundred li along the Yellow River from Daning to Gu Town the waters ran clear from the eighth of the month until the tenth, as before.

sentences.zh: 九月辛丑，西京大內放出兩宮內人及前朝宮人，任其所適。

translations.literal: On xinchou of the ninth month the Western Capital's inner palace released palace women of the two palaces and former dynasty palace women, free to go where they would.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the Western Capital released inner-palace women and women of the former dynasty to go where they wished.

sentences.zh: 敕以近年文武官諸道奉使，皆於所在分外停住，逾年涉歲，未聞歸闕。

translations.literal: An edict said that in recent years civil and military officials on missions from the circuits all stayed extra at their posts beyond measure, for years without returning to court.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that civil and military envoys from the circuits lately lingered at post for years without returning.

sentences.zh: 非惟勞費州郡，抑且侮慢國經。

translations.literal: Not only did this waste prefectures and counties—it also insulted the state's institutions.
translations.idiomatic: They wasted local resources and slighted the state's order.

sentences.zh: 臣節既虧，憲章安在。

translations.literal: If ministerial integrity is lacking, where is the constitution?
translations.idiomatic: Where integrity fails, law cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 自今後兩浙、福建、廣州、安南、邕、容等道使到發許住一月；

translations.literal: From now on envoys to the two Zhes, Fujian, Guangzhou, Annan, Yong, and Rong may stay one month;
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth envoys to the two Zhes, Fujian, Guangzhou, Annan, Yong, and Rong may stay one month;

sentences.zh: 湖南、洪、鄂、黔、桂許住二十日；

translations.literal: Hunan, Hong, E, Qian, and Gui may stay twenty days;
translations.idiomatic: Hunan, Hong, E, Qian, and Gui twenty days;

sentences.zh: 荊、襄、同、雍、鎮、定、青、滄許住十日；

translations.literal: Jing, Xiang, Tong, Yong, Zhen, Ding, Qing, and Cang may stay ten days;
translations.idiomatic: Jing, Xiang, Tong, Yong, Zhen, Ding, Qing, and Cang ten days;

sentences.zh: 其餘側近不過三五日。

translations.literal: the rest nearby no more than three to five days.
translations.idiomatic: nearby circuits no more than three to five.

sentences.zh: 凡往來道路，據遠近里數，日行兩驛。

translations.literal: On roads coming and going, according to distance in li, travel two post-stages per day.
translations.idiomatic: On the road, measure by distance and travel two relay-stages a day.

sentences.zh: 如遇疾患及江河阻隔，委所在長吏具事由奏聞。

translations.literal: If illness or rivers and barriers intervene, let the local magistrate report the circumstances by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Sickness or rivers may delay travel—local magistrates shall report by memorial.

sentences.zh: 如或有違，當行朝典，命御史點檢糾察，以儆慢官。

translations.literal: If there is violation, the court code shall be applied; censors are ordered to inspect and correct, to warn negligent officials.
translations.idiomatic: Violators face the court code; censors shall inspect and punish the negligent.

sentences.zh: 魏博羅紹威二男廷望、廷矩，年在幼稚，皆有材器，帝以其籓屏勳臣之胄，宜受非次之用，皆擢為郎。

translations.literal: Luo Shaowei of Weibo's two sons Tingwang and Tingju, though still young, both had talent; the Emperor, because they were scions of a meritorious screen-vassal, deserved extraordinary employment—both were promoted to court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei's sons Tingwang and Tingju, though young, showed talent; as sons of a loyal frontier lord both were made court gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 恩命既行之後，二子亦就班列。

translations.literal: After the favor was granted, the two sons also took their places in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: After the edict they took their places in court ranks.

sentences.zh: 紹威乃上章，以齒幼未任公事，乞免主印、宿直。

translations.literal: Shaowei then submitted a memorial that, being young in years, they were not yet fit for public business, and begged exemption from holding seals and night duty.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei then asked that, being young, they be excused seals and night duty.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 封鎮東軍神祠為崇福侯。

translations.literal: The shrine of the Zhendong Army was enfeoffed as the Marquis of Chongfu.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhendong Army shrine was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chongfu.

sentences.zh: 浙西奏，道門威儀鄭章、道士夏隱言，焚修精志，妙達希夷，推諸輩流實有道業。

translations.literal: The Western Zhe circuit reported that Daoist master of rites Zheng Zhang and priest Xia Yinyan burned incense in refined aspiration, wonderfully attained the rare and remote, and among their peers truly had the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Western Zhe reported that ritual master Zheng Zhang and priest Xia Yinyan, in refined devotion, had truly attained the Way among their peers.

sentences.zh: 鄭章宜賜號貞一大師，仍名元章，隱言賜紫衣。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhang should be granted the title Great Master of Perfect Unity, with the name Yuanzhang; Yinyan should be granted purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhang was titled Great Master of Perfect Unity with the name Yuanzhang; Yinyan received purple robes.

sentences.zh: 〈《五代會要》：九月，置左右天興、左右廣勝軍，仍以親王為軍使。〉

translations.literal: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: In the ninth month the Left and Right Tianxing and Left and Right Guangsheng Armies were established, with imperial princes as army commissioners.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records: In the ninth month the Left and Right Tianxing and Guangsheng Armies were created, led by imperial princes.〉

sentences.zh: 十月，帝以用軍，未暇西幸，文武百官等久居東京，漸及疑訝，令就便各許歸安，只留韓建、薛貽矩，翰林學士張策、韋郊、杜曉，中書舍人封舜聊、張袞並左右御史、司天監、宗正寺，兼要當諸司節級外，其宰臣張文蔚已下文武百官，並先於西京祗候。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, because the Emperor was using the army and had no leisure to visit the west, civil and military officials long dwelling in the Eastern Capital gradually grew doubtful; he ordered that each might return home as convenient, retaining only Han Jian, Xue Yiju, Hanlin academicians Zhang Ce, Wei Jiao, and Du Xiao, Secretariat drafters Feng Shunliao and Zhang Gun, and the Left and Right Censors, Directorate of Astronomy, and Court of Imperial Clan, together with essential bureau chiefs—while chief ministers from Zhang Wenwei down and all civil and military officials should first wait in attendance at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, busy with war and unable to go west, the Emperor let officials long in the Eastern Capital return home on leave, keeping only Han Jian, Xue Yiju, Zhang Ce, Wei Jiao, Du Xiao, Feng Shunliao, Zhang Gun, censors, the astronomical directorate, and the imperial clan office—while Zhang Wenwei and the rest were to wait at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 庚午，大明節，內外臣僚各以奇貨良馬上壽。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Great Brightness Festival, inner and outer officials each presented rare goods and fine horses in congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the Great Brightness Festival, officials within and without offered rare goods and fine horses.

sentences.zh: 故事，內殿開宴，召釋、道二教對禦談論，宣旨罷之。

translations.literal: By precedent, at inner banquets Buddhist and Daoist clergy were summoned to discourse before the throne; an edict ended the practice.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom inner banquets summoned Buddhist and Daoist debate before the throne; an edict ended it.

sentences.zh: 命閣門使以香合賜宰臣佛寺行香。

translations.literal: The gate commissioner was ordered to bestow incense boxes on chief ministers for offering incense at Buddhist temples.
translations.idiomatic: Gate commissioners were told to give chief ministers incense boxes for temple offerings.

sentences.zh: 駕幸繁台講武。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage visited Fantai to review troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor reviewed troops at Fantai.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，御史司憲薛廷圭奏請文武百官仍舊朝參。

translations.literal: On guiyou Xue Tinggui, director of the Censorate, memorialized requesting that civil and military officials resume regular court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou Censor-in-Chief Xue Tinggui asked that civil and military officials resume regular court.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝欲親征河東，命朝臣先赴洛都，至是緩其期，乃允所奏。

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had wished to campaign in person against Hedong and ordered court officials to go first to Luoyang; now he delayed the date and granted the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had meant to campaign east against Hedong and sent the court ahead to Luoyang; he now delayed and granted the request.

sentences.zh: 宰臣請每月初入閣，望日延英聽政，永為常式。

translations.literal: Chief ministers requested that on the first entry to the palace each month and on audience days at Yanying Hall governance be heard—perpetually as a fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers asked that on the first palace entry each month and on Yanying audience days policy be heard—as a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使楊師厚進納越匡凝東第書籍。

translations.literal: Yang Shihou, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, presented and surrendered the books of Yue Kuangning's eastern mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shihou of Shannan East surrendered the library of Yue Kuangning's eastern mansion.

sentences.zh: 先是，收復襄、漢，帝閱其圖書，至是命師厚進焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiang and Han were recovered, the Emperor had examined these books; now he ordered Shihou to present them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangyang and Hanzhong were retaken the Emperor had browsed these books; now he ordered Shihou to deliver them.

sentences.zh: 廣州進獻助軍錢二十萬，又進龍腦、腰帶、珍珠枕、玳瑁、香藥等。

translations.literal: Guangzhou presented two hundred thousand in military-aid money, and also presented dragon-brain, belts, pearl pillows, tortoiseshell, and fragrant medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou sent two hundred thousand in military aid plus dragon-brain, belts, pearl pillows, tortoiseshell, and aromatics.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬寅，帝以征討未罷，調補為先，遂命盡赦逃亡背役髡黥之人，各許歸鄉里。

translations.literal: On renyin of the eleventh month, because the campaign was not yet ended and replacements came first, an order was issued to pardon entirely those who had fled, deserted service, or been tattooed and shaved, each permitted to return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, with war unfinished and levies urgent, the Emperor pardoned deserters, draft-dodgers, and branded convicts to return home.

sentences.zh: 廣州進龍形通犀腰帶、金托裏含稜玳瑁器百餘副，香藥珍巧甚多。

translations.literal: Guangzhou presented dragon-patterned rhinoceros-horn belts, more than a hundred sets of gold-mounted inlaid tortoiseshell vessels, and very many fragrant medicines and ingenious objects.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou sent dragon-pattern rhinoceros belts, a hundred-odd gold-mounted tortoiseshell sets, and countless aromatics and curios.

sentences.zh: 廣南管內獲白鹿，並圖形來獻，耳有兩缺。

translations.literal: Within the Guangnan circuit a white deer was captured; its form was diagrammed and presented, its ears having two notches.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnan captured a white deer, diagrammed and sent to court, its ears notched twice.

sentences.zh: 按《符瑞圖》，鹿壽千歲變白，耳一缺。

translations.literal: According to the 《Records of Omens》, when a deer lives a thousand years it turns white and its ear has one notch.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Records of Omens》 says a deer of a thousand years turns white and its ear has one notch.

sentences.zh: 今驗此鹿耳有二缺，其獸與色皆應金行，實表嘉瑞。

translations.literal: Now examining this deer, its ears had two notches; beast and color both answered the Metal phase—truly a sign of auspicious fortune.
translations.idiomatic: This deer's two notches and white coat matched the Metal phase—a true omen of blessing.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛亥，詔曰：「潞寇未平，王師在野。

translations.literal: On xinhai of the twelfth month an edict said: "The Luzhou rebels are not yet pacified; the royal army is in the field.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai an edict said: "Luzhou is not yet pacified; the royal army is in the field.

sentences.zh: 攻戰之勢，難緩於寇圍；

translations.literal: The momentum of attack is hard to slacken before the rebels' encirclement;
translations.idiomatic: Attack cannot slacken while the enemy is ringed;

sentences.zh: 飛晳免之勤，實勞於人力。

translations.literal: the diligence of flying grain and night watches truly wearies human strength.
translations.idiomatic: grain convoys and night watches wear men out."

sentences.zh: 永言輟耒，深用軫懷。

translations.literal: Ever mindful of the halted plow, I am deeply moved in my breast.
translations.idiomatic: "I grieve for the idle plow.

sentences.zh: 宜令長吏，丁寧佈告，期以兵罷之日，給復賦租。

translations.literal: Let local magistrates earnestly proclaim: when the army withdraws, tax and corvée shall be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Let magistrates proclaim: when the army stands down, taxes and corvée will be remitted."

sentences.zh: 」於是人戶聞之，皆忘其倦。

translations.literal: When households heard this, they all forgot their weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing it, the people took heart.

sentences.zh: 詔故荊南節度使、守中書令、上谷王周汭贈太師，故武昌軍節度使、兼中書令、西平王杜洪贈太傅。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously honored the former military governor of Jingnan, Defender of the Secretariat and Prince of Shanggu Wang Zhou, as Grand Preceptor, and the former military governor of Wuchang, Concurrent Secretariat Director and Prince of Xiping Du Hong, as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou of Jingnan, late Prince of Shanggu, was posthumously made Grand Preceptor; Du Hong of Wuchang, late Prince of Xiping, Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 先是，鄂渚再為淮夷所侵，攻圍甚急，杜洪以兵食將盡，繼來乞師。

translations.literal: Earlier Ezhou had again been invaded by Huai barbarians; the siege was very urgent, and Du Hong repeatedly came begging for troops as grain was nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Ezhou had again been harried by Huai foes; Du Hong, grain nearly gone, begged repeatedly for relief.

sentences.zh: 帝料其隔越大江，難以赴援，兼以荊州據上游，多戰艦，去江夏甚邇，因命周汭舉舟師沿流以救之。

translations.literal: The Emperor judged that crossing the great Yangzi was hard to aid in time; moreover Jingzhou lay on the upper stream with many war vessels, very close to Jiangxia—hence he ordered Zhou Yu to raise a fleet and go downriver to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged the Yangzi too wide for timely aid; Jingzhou upstream had many warships and lay near Jiangxia—so he ordered Zhou Yu downriver by fleet.

sentences.zh: 汭於是引兵東下，才及鄂界，遇朗州背盟作亂，乘江陵之虛，縱兵襲破之，俘掠且盡。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon led troops east; just reaching the border of E, he met Langzhou breaking faith and rising in revolt, exploiting Jiangling's emptiness to raid and break it, plundering nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Yu marched east; at E's border Langzhou broke faith, struck empty Jiangling, and plundered it bare.

sentences.zh: 既而汭士卒知之，皆顧其家，咸無鬥志，遂為淮寇所敗，將卒潰散，汭忿恚自投于江。

translations.literal: When Yu's soldiers learned of it, they all looked to their homes and had no will to fight; they were defeated by Huai bandits, officers and men scattered; Yu in rage and grief threw himself into the river.
translations.idiomatic: His men thought only of home and would not fight; Huai raiders routed them; Yu drowned himself in grief.

sentences.zh: 汭之本姓犯文穆皇帝廟諱，至是因追贈，以其系出周文，故賜姓周氏。

translations.literal: Yu's original surname violated the temple taboo of Emperor Wenmu; now because of the posthumous gift, since his line came from the Zhou of Wen, he was granted the surname Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's birth surname violated Emperor Wenmu's taboo; on posthumous honor, as his line came from King Wen of Zhou, he was granted the surname Zhou.

sentences.zh: 及汭兵敗之後，武昌以重圍經年，糧盡力困，救援不至，訖為淮寇所陷，載洪以送淮師，遂殺之。

translations.literal: After Yu's army was defeated, Wuchang, besieged for years with grain exhausted and relief not arriving, in the end was taken by Huai bandits, who carried Hong off to the Huai army and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu's defeat Wuchang, besieged for years without relief, fell to Huai raiders who carried Hong away and killed him.

sentences.zh: 此二鎮，皆以忠貞歿于王事。

translations.literal: These two circuits both died loyal in the king's service.
translations.idiomatic: Both circuits died loyal in royal service.

sentences.zh: 帝每言諸籓屏翰經綸之業，必首痛汭、洪之薨，至是追贈之，深加軫悼，各以其子孫宗屬錄用焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor spoke of the frontier lords' tasks of statecraft, he always first grieved Yu and Hong's deaths; now he posthumously honored them, deeply lamenting, and employed their sons and clan kindred.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor always grieved Zhou and Du first when he spoke of frontier duty; now he honored them posthumously and employed their kin.

sentences.zh: 棣州蒲台縣百姓王知嚴妹，以亂離並失怙恃，因舉哀追感，自截兩指以祭父母。

translations.literal: Wang Zhiyan's sister of Putai County in Dizhou, because of disorder and separation, had lost both parents; in mourning and grief she cut off two fingers to sacrifice to her parents.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhiyan's sister of Dizhou's Putai, orphaned in chaos, mourned her parents and cut off two fingers as offering.

sentences.zh: 帝以遺體之重，不合毀傷，言念村閭，何知禮教。

translations.literal: The Emperor said that the body received from parents must not be harmed; thinking of village folk, how would they know ritual teaching?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said the body is a gift of parents and must not be maimed—villagers know no better ritual.

sentences.zh: 自今後所在郡縣，如有截指割股，不用奏聞。

translations.literal: From now on wherever in prefectures and counties anyone cuts fingers or flesh from the thigh, do not memorialize it.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth local officials need not report finger-cutting or thigh-flesh offerings.

sentences.zh: 是年，諸道多奏軍人百姓割股，青、齊、河朔尤多。

translations.literal: That year many circuits memorialized that soldiers and commoners cut flesh from the thigh; Qing, Qi, and the Hebei region especially had many.
translations.idiomatic: That year many circuits reported soldiers and peasants cutting thigh-flesh; Qing, Qi, and Hebei had the most.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此若因心，亦足為孝。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If this comes from the heart, it is enough to count as filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "If it comes from the heart, it may count as filial.

sentences.zh: 但苟免徭役，自殘肌膚，欲以庇身，何能療疾？

translations.literal: But if it is only to escape corvée, mutilating one's flesh—wishing to shield the body, how can it cure illness?
translations.idiomatic: But to dodge corvée by maiming oneself—how does that heal anyone?

sentences.zh: 並宜止絕。」

translations.literal: Let it all be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Let it all cease."

sentences.zh: 〈《五代會要》：十二月，於輝州碭山縣置崇德軍。

translations.literal: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: In the twelfth month the Chongde Army was established in Dangshan County, Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records: In the twelfth month the Chongde Army was set up in Huizhou's Dangshan County.

sentences.zh: 太祖榆社在碭山，置使以領之，始命朱彥讓為軍使。〉

translations.literal: The Taizu's elm community was in Dangshan; a commissioner was placed to administer it, and Zhu Yanrang was first appointed army commissioner.〉
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's ancestral elm grove lay in Dangshan; a commissioner was appointed to oversee it, and Zhu Yanrang was first named army commissioner.〉
